items.title: Fix nocopy values decoded from streams
items.body:
## Summary

- allocate stable slices when decoding from generic streams
- add a regression test for adjacent short `nocopy.String` fields

## Root cause

`streamReader.Slice` reused one 10-byte scratch buffer. `nocopy.String` and other retained nocopy codecs alias the returned slice, so decoding the next short value overwrote earlier values. Generic streams have no reusable backing buffer, so each retained slice must own its bytes. Slice-backed `Unmarshal` remains zero-copy.

## Reproduction

Before the fix, decoding `{First: "first", Second: "second"}` through `NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(...))` produced `{First: "secon", Second: "second"}`.

## Benchmarks

Apple M2, Go 1.25, 10 runs for the targeted benchmark. The pre-fix result is fast because it aliases mutable scratch memory and is incorrect.

| benchmark | master | fix | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| two short `nocopy.String` values via stream | 39.42 ns/op, 0 B, 0 allocs | 53.32 ns/op, 16 B, 2 allocs | +35.3%, +2 required allocations |
| repository `binary/stream-dec` | 132.6 ns/op, 1 alloc | 138.2 ns/op, 2 allocs | +4.2%, +1 allocation |
| slice-backed `nocopy/str-dec` | 32.0 ns/op, 0 allocs | 31.9 ns/op, 0 allocs | unchanged |

Full repository benchmark suite: `cd bench && go run .` (100 samples, 10 ms/sample).

## Checks

- `go test ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `git diff --check`

items.title: Pin `mqt-bench==2.2.2` and Update `_benchmark_names.py` + Generator
items.body:
The contents of `_benchmark_names.py` depend on the exact version of **`mqt‑bench`** that was used to generate it. When a different version is installed, the module contains incorrect benchmark names, causing test failures.

In the CI for Graphix (a reverse dependency), this problem manifested because the file had been generated with `mqt-bench==2.1.0`, while `pyproject.toml` only required `mqt‑bench>=2.1.0`. Consequently, CI installed the newer release **2.2.2**, leading to a mismatch.

For instance, see https://github.com/TeamGraphix/graphix/actions/runs/28994040306/job/86039809250?pr=558

**Fixes introduced in this commit:**
- Pin the `mqt-bench` dependency to version **2.2.2**.
- Enable Dependabot to keep this pin up‑to‑date when necessary.
- Add a generator script that can recreate `_benchmark_names.py` for any future `mqt-bench` version.
- Run the generator with the new pinned version and commit the updated `_benchmark_names.py`.

These changes ensure that the benchmark names stay in sync with the installed `mqt-bench` version, preventing CI failures.

items.title: Restore the paper nonsmooth optimization flow
items.body:
### Motivation

- The C++ solver diverged from the paper by using a normalized objective, non-paper step rule, PR+ clipping, missing per-stage best snapshots, and incorrect coarse-net construction, which caused history/summary/final.pl inconsistencies and incorrect benchmark tagging.
- The change restores the original paper semantics so final outputs, history, and summary are authoritative and comparable to the paper-mode reference.

### Description

- Replace normalized objective and density scaling with raw paper objective `W + lambda * P`, make density penalty equal to the per-bin squared positive overflow and emit gradients in area units (changes in `src/objective/Density.cpp`).
- Implement paper-mode optimizer math: L1-balanced initial `lambda = ||g_W||_1 / ||g_P||_1`, unclipped Polak–Ribiere beta, paper step schedule `alpha = s * bin_width / ||d||_2` with `s` multiplied by `2/3` every 100 iters and floor `0.06`, per-stage best-so-far snapshots and restore, OFR-driven lambda growth (1.6/1.9/2.2) and no-improvement stopping (`src/optimizer/NonsmoothOptimizer.cpp`, `include/placer/optimizer/NonsmoothOptimizer.hpp`).
- Fix multilevel contraction to deduplicate coarse incidences and drop internal nets (so coarse net counts reflect true contraction) and ensure decluster uses the authoritative optimized coarse state (`src/multilevel/Clusterer.cpp`).
- Unify reporting and outputs: history CSV fields were reworked to raw fields and expanded diagnostics, `summary.json` and `run_info.json` now record `benchmark_name` and AUX path and summary is produced from the authoritative DB/level (changes in `src/io/Reporter.cpp`, `include/placer/io/Reporter.hpp`, `app/main.cpp`).
- Add `--expected-benchmark` to validate the AUX matches the claimed benchmark, add docs with an audit and solver conventions, add unit tests for paper math and adjust tiny end-to-end test to assert new history header (`tests/*`, `docs/*`).

### Testing

- Configured and built with CMake and Ninja in Debug and Release modes and ran unit tests, with `ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure` reporting 100% (16/16) tests passed after adjustments.
- Ran tiny end-to-end smoke (`tests/data/tiny/tiny_basic`) and verified `history.csv` contains the new `raw_objective` header and does not contain the old `total_norm` field, and produced expected output files.
- Verified benchmark identity enforcement by invoking the binary with `--expected-benchmark` mismatching the AUX and confirmed it errors with non-zero exit code, and ran an adaptec1 two-stage smoke run to validate coarse contraction, lambda staging, and output consistency.

items.title: fix(run_stats): normalize through int64_t microseconds (backport #463/#465 to 2.4)
items.body:
Backport of #463/#465 to the **2.4 release branch**, for inclusion in 2.4.4.

## Why

`run_stats::timeval_factorial_average` averaged `tv_sec` and `tv_usec` independently with `double`→`time_t`/`suseconds_t` truncation. For aggregate durations < ~1ms across multiple clients, the diff could round to **0 µs**, making `summarize()` report **Ops/sec = 0** (and Hits/sec, KB/sec) even when `Count > 0` and `Avg Latency > 0`. That's a user-facing results-correctness bug — exactly what a patch release should carry.

## Fix

Normalize both timevals to `int64_t` microseconds, average via integer math, split back. No precision loss for any aggregate duration > 0 µs. 8-line change, cherry-picked cleanly from master (`b4b18c0`).

Found during the 2.4.4 release-contents audit: this was the one correctness fix on `master` since 2.4.3 that was missing from `2.4` and applies cleanly.

items.title: fix(benchmark): capture warmup end time before benchmark phase
items.body:
## Bug
Warmup duration in benchmark results was incorrect. It showed ~5500 ms for `--benchmark-fast` (500ms warmup + 5000ms benchmark + processing). The reported warmup time included the entire benchmark phase.

## Root cause
`warmup_duration_ms` was calculated as:
```c
result->warmup_duration_ms = (int)(get_microseconds() - warmup_start) / 1000;
```
But `get_microseconds()` was called at line 156, **after** the benchmark phase completed. So it captured warmup + benchmark + result processing time.

## Fix
Capture `warmup_end = get_microseconds()` immediately after the warmup loop ends (line 110), before the benchmark phase starts. Use `warmup_end - warmup_start` for the warmup duration report.

## Before/After
| | Warmup reported | Actual warmup |
|---|---|---|
| Before | ~5501 ms | 500 ms |
| After | 500 ms | 500 ms |

**Do not merge without explicit approval.**

items.title: fix(build): decouple time-gating from allocation-gating in BenchCheck
items.body:
D-395 found BenchCheck's ×3σ per-sprint time filter is blind to between-run variance, and diagnosed a trap in fixing it: policy.json's "gating" flag coupled compile's time axis to its allocation-percent axis, so silencing time would have silenced the allocation-percent check too, even though allocation is deterministic and demonstrably had a 0.0% delta on the run that broke main.

ClassifyTime no longer takes a gating/CPU/Policy parameter at all - it always returns TimeClass.Informational, so no category can gate on time by construction rather than by a flag reading false. The now-unreachable Ok/CpuMismatch/PerSprintBreach/CumulativeBreach TimeClass values are removed. PolicyCategory.Gating is renamed AllocGating (JSON gating -> allocGating) and scoped to the allocation-percent axis alone, mirroring D-391's ceiling precedent (gates regardless of any flag) while staying per-category, since the gating matrix keeps allocation-percent scoped to compile only.

items.title: Add zero-copy tensor fabric and transport benchmarks
items.body:
## What changed

- Reworked `Tensor` into a cheap copyable handle over shared move-only device storage.
- Added explicit shape, stride, offset, storage identity, bounds-checked views, and contiguous-layout detection.
- Added `TensorHandle` readiness events and `TensorFabric` routing.
- Same-device routes now preserve the exact backing allocation and data pointer while submitting only producer-to-consumer event dependencies.
- Added explicit route modes and copied-byte accounting so expensive fallbacks cannot be hidden.
- Added correctness-first CPU -> CUDA and CUDA -> CPU routes.
- Added CUDA event synchronization support to the device contract.
- Added real CUDA hardware tests for H2D, zero-copy handoff, stream/event ordering, D2H byte-exact verification, 1,000 repeated handoffs, CUDA -> CPU, and CPU -> CUDA routing.
- Added `tgraft_bench`, a transport benchmark comparing zero-copy handoff against D2D copy and GPU -> CPU -> GPU staging.
- Added benchmark methodology and claim-scoping documentation.
- Bumped the development version to 0.3.0.

## Why

This is the first TensorGraft layer that implements the core product hypothesis directly: an intermediate tensor produced on a device can be consumed by another stage on the same device without copying its payload or synchronizing the host. The handoff preserves storage lifetime through shared ownership and preserves execution correctness through backend events.

## Correctness model

- Same-device: zero-copy alias + consumer stream waits on producer event.
- CPU -> CUDA: destination CUDA allocation + CUDA-stream copy + destination readiness event.
- CUDA -> CPU: CUDA transfer stream + synchronized correctness-first fallback.
- Multi-GPU: deliberately rejected until peer-access capability and topology negotiation exist.
- Cross-device copies currently require contiguous tensors; unsupported layouts fail explicitly instead of silently copying incorrect bytes.

## Benchmark discipline

`tgraft_bench` validates a deterministic 32 MiB tensor byte-for-byte before printing performance numbers. It reports transport-only latency/bandwidth and clearly labels the resulting ratios as transport-layer results, not end-to-end model speedup claims.

## Validation

- The PR CI builds and tests CPU paths on Ubuntu and Windows and also compiles the benchmark target.
- CUDA-enabled tests are compiled and executed when a real CUDA Toolkit/GPU environment is used.
- The intended hardware validation target is Windows + CUDA 13.3 + the repository owner's NVIDIA GPU, where the previous CUDA backend already compiled and initialized successfully.

This PR should remain draft until both CI and the real CUDA hardware test/benchmark pass.

items.title: fix(dates): stop initialize_placeholder_map from re-deriving a single shared year
items.body:
## Summary

`initialize_placeholder_map()` (`navi_bench/dates.py`) feeds ground-truth date resolution for resy, opentable, and google_flights task generation. Its string-parsed branch discarded the already-correct calendar year(s) that `parse_relative_date(s)` computed and instead re-derived a **single shared year for the whole resolved list** via "normalize every date to `base_date.year`, then bump every date to `base_date.year + 1` if the earliest one is on or before `base_date`".

This is the same "hand-rolled year rollover instead of trusting the already-correct resolution" bug pattern already fixed elsewhere in this module (#144/#145/#151), but here it silently **corrupted** resolved dates instead of crashing:

- A `"from <A> through <B>"` range spanning a Dec → Jan boundary (e.g. `"Dec 27 through Jan 10"`) got every date's year collapsed onto one re-derived year, producing a self-contradictory span (December dates ending up *after* January dates).
- Any `"this month"`/`"this <weekday>"` list containing even one date before `base_date` (e.g. `"weekends in this month"` once the month's first weekend has passed) got its **entire** list — including the still-upcoming dates — pushed a full year forward, since the bump decision only looked at the earliest date.
- A `"last X"` resolution that correctly lands in the year before `base_date`'s year got silently forced back into `base_date`'s year, since the old code only ever bumped forward, never backward.

This function had **zero prior test coverage** despite being the shared placeholder-date resolver for three domains.

## Fix

Keep the dates `parse_relative_date(s)` already resolved as-is, and only look at their years to decide whether to append a disambiguating `", {year}"` suffix to the rendered task description. No re-derivation, no overwriting.

## Verification

- Parity check against the old reconstruction logic across ~3000 randomized (description, base_date) pairs: old and new agree exactly whenever the resolved list shares a single year equal to `base_date`'s year or `base_date`'s year + 1 (the common forward-bump case, ~1900/2800 sampled combos), and diverge everywhere else (~830 combos), with the new code matching the trusted `parse_relative_date(s)` output in every diverging case.
- Added `tests/test_dates.py` (new file — this function had no prior coverage) with 5 characterization tests: 3 reproduce the bug (year-spanning range, partially-past "this month", backward "last X") and were confirmed to **fail against the pre-fix code via `git stash`**; 2 pin the unaffected common forward-bump happy path (with and without the year-disambiguation suffix) to confirm no regression there.
- `pytest tests/` (excluding `test_vis.py`, which needs the private `yutori` package): 179 → 184 passed.
- `ruff check` clean on both changed files. (`ruff format --check` flags one pre-existing, unrelated line in `navi_bench/dates.py` that predates this change — confirmed via `git stash` against `main` — left untouched to keep this diff minimal.)

items.title: Implement CacheForge Milestone 1 attention runtime and contiguous KV cache
items.body:
This PR adds the first educational runtime slice of CacheForge: a minimal PyTorch implementation of Llama-style causal self-attention with RoPE, grouped-query attention, and a preallocated contiguous KV cache. It also adds the supporting package layout, deterministic correctness tests, a decode microbenchmark, and README documentation for the full-context vs cached decode comparison.

- **Package + configuration**
  - Adds a `src/`-layout `cacheforge` package with installable project metadata in `pyproject.toml`
  - Introduces `AttentionConfig` validation for:
    - head divisibility
    - GQA ratio (`num_attention_heads % num_key_value_heads == 0`)
    - even `head_dim` for RoPE
    - bounded `max_seq_len`

- **Attention runtime**
  - Implements Llama-style causal self-attention in `src/cacheforge/attention.py`
  - Supports:
    - full-context forward without cache
    - prompt prefill into cache
    - single-token decode against cached history
    - GQA with KV expansion only at attention time, not in cache storage
  - Applies RoPE using absolute positions for both prompt and decode paths

- **RoPE**
  - Adds a small standalone rotary embedding implementation in `src/cacheforge/rope.py`
  - Validates tensor/position shapes explicitly to keep failure modes clear

- **Contiguous KV cache**
  - Adds `ContiguousKVCache` with preallocated `[batch, num_kv_heads, max_seq_len, head_dim]` storage for K and V
  - Supports:
    - multi-token range writes for prefill
    - explicit-position single-token appends for decode
    - per-slot lengths
    - slot reset / full reset
    - exact allocated-byte reporting from backing storage
  - Rejects invalid shapes, dtypes, devices, out-of-bounds writes, and unwritten gaps

- **Correctness coverage**
  - Adds deterministic pytest coverage for:
    - multi-token write + one-token append
    - slot isolation across batch entries
    - bounds / invalid-shape errors
    - reset and reuse
    - theoretical vs actual KV allocation bytes
    - full-context vs prefill+decode numerical equivalence
    - GQA shape/equivalence behavior
    - decode-position handling that would fail if RoPE were incorrectly reset

- **Benchmark + docs**
  - Adds `benchmarks/benchmark_decode.py` to compare full recomputation per step vs prefill + cached decode
  - Exposes CLI controls for device, dtype, prompt length, decode steps, warmup, and repeats
  - Reports:
    - latency table
    - theoretical KV bytes
    - actual allocated KV bytes
    - CUDA peak allocation when CUDA is used
  - Expands `README.md` with tensor-shape walkthroughs, cache memory formula, prefill vs decode behavior, and current milestone boundaries

Example usage:

```python
import torch

from cacheforge.attention import LlamaSelfAttention
from cacheforge.cache.contiguous import ContiguousKVCache
from cacheforge.config import AttentionConfig

config = AttentionConfig(
    hidden_size=128,
    num_attention_heads=8,
    num_key_value_heads=2,
    max_seq_len=64,
)

attn = LlamaSelfAttention(config).eval()
cache = ContiguousKVCache(
    batch_size=1,
    num_kv_heads=config.num_key_value_heads,
    max_seq_len=config.max_seq_len,
    head_dim=config.head_dim,
    dtype=torch.float32,
    device="cpu",
)

prompt = torch.randn(1, 16, config.hidden_size)
_ = attn.prefill(prompt, cache)

next_token = torch.randn(1, 1, config.hidden_size)
out = attn.decode(next_token, cache, positions=torch.tensor([[16]]))
```

items.body:
## Summary

This PR hardens the core Raft and LSM paths that were exposed by long-running production-style E2E tests. It fixes lost apply notifications, incorrect benchmark commit-channel handling, LSM SSTable publication/recovery edge cases, manager-local LSM ID allocation, durable Raft commit-index recovery, and WAL recovery hygiene.

Closes #102.
Closes #103.
Closes #104.
Closes #105.
Closes #106.
Closes #107.

## Design Notes

### Raft apply and restart safety

- `commitChan` notifications are no longer dropped when the channel is full. The apply path now blocks until the notification is delivered or shutdown begins.
- Performance harnesses now only drain `commitChan`; they do not apply already-applied entries a second time.
- `HardState.CommitIndex` is restored on restart and persisted when leaders/followers advance commit index. This is an implementation guardrail for this repository's persistent state machine; it does not change the Raft quorum commit rule.
- `Stop()` now waits for in-flight apply, snapshot, AppendEntries, and state-machine/storage critical sections before callers close or reopen storage.
- Stopped nodes reject RequestVote, AppendEntries acknowledgement, and InstallSnapshot paths instead of participating after shutdown starts.

### LSM SSTable and WAL recovery

- SSTable `EncodeTo` now publishes through a same-directory temp file, `Sync`, `Close`, and `Rename` before metadata is published.
- Empty immutable memtables are skipped instead of becoming empty Level-0 SSTables.
- SSTable recovery ignores uncommitted temp files and removes legacy empty SSTables.
- Empty SSTables do not pass size `0` into the generic `DataBlock.DecodeFrom` API, because size `0` means unlimited at that layer.
- SSTable and MemTable IDs are now manager-local. Recovering one database no longer resets a package-level generator used by another live database.
- MemTable recovery only replays committed `{id}.wal` files, ignores non-WAL directory entries, and still fails on corrupt committed WAL files.

### Documentation

- Updated English and Chinese design docs for Raft, LSM, and system recovery boundaries.
- Updated the bug-fix retrospective with #102-#107 root causes, core principles, code snippets, and validation notes.
- Updated the performance report with the latest June 22, 2026 long-running E2E results.

items.body:
Clamp early-final TTFS to 0, record non-comparable (cold/non-HTTP2) TTFA as a null-valued success, and give the runner a writable cache dir so runs stop going partial or warning on benign edges.

Greptile Summary

This PR addresses three distinct edge cases that were incorrectly flipping benchmark runs to `PARTIAL`: an early STT final clamping to 0 instead of raising, contaminated TTFA rows being marked `FAILED` instead of null-valued `SUCCESS`, and the cache directory being unwritable for the nonroot container user. - **TTFS clamping** (`ttft.py`): `compute_ttfs` now returns `max(0.0, ...)` rather than raising `ValueError` when the final arrives ahead of the speech-end anchor; the `0.0` propagates as a valid `SUCCESS` row instead of a caught exception that nulls the value and can chain to a `PARTIAL` run. - **TTFA contamination gate** (`orchestrator.py`): HTTP/1.1 and cold-socket TTFA measurements no longer flip `ttfa_status` to `FAILED`; they remain `SUCCESS` with `metric_value=None` (excluded from aggregation) so a WER-only success still finishes the run as `SUCCEEDED`. - **Docker cache dir** (`Dockerfile`): `XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp` routes dataset cache writes to `/tmp`, which is always writable by the nonroot uid `65532`.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge. All three changes are well-scoped, well-tested, and address genuine false-positive failures rather than altering measurement semantics. The TTFS clamp, TTFA null-valued-success conversion, and cache-dir fix are each minimal and independently correct. The `_metric_outcome` identity check (`is None`) handles 0.0 correctly, the transport-contamination gate correctly preserves `ttfa_status=SUCCESS` while nulling the value, and the run-level aggregation (`status == FAILED` counts) is unaffected. items.title: unixbench release 6.0.1
items.body:
Changes

  Build System

  - Specify C standard (Makefile): Added -std=gnu89 -Wno-declaration-after-statement to CFLAGS. Fixes compilation failures on GCC 15+ and Clang 21+ where
  implicit function declarations and K&R-style definitions are no longer accepted by default. (#125 (https://github.com/kdlucas/byte-unixbench/pull/125))

  Compiler Optimization and Link-Time Optimization (LTO) Fixes

  - Prevent loop counters from being optimized away (arith.c was already volatile): Added volatile qualifier to global benchmark iteration counters in
  dhry_1.c, hanoi.c, syscall.c, pipe.c, context1.c, spawn.c, and looper.c. These variables are incremented in tight loops and read asynchronously by SIGALRM
   signal handlers. Without volatile, LTO and aggressive optimizers (GCC 15+, Clang 21+) may eliminate the loops entirely or cache stale register values,
  producing zero or incorrect benchmark scores. (#122 (https://github.com/kdlucas/byte-unixbench/pull/122))

  Printf Format String Fixes

  - Fix %ld → %lu for unsigned long variables across 6 files (arith.c, dhry_1.c, hanoi.c, pipe.c, syscall.c, fstime.c). Using %ld (signed) for unsigned long
   arguments is undefined behavior per the C standard. On some platforms this caused garbled or negative iteration counts in COUNT| output, corrupting
  benchmark results. (#126 (https://github.com/kdlucas/byte-unixbench/pull/126), #127 (https://github.com/kdlucas/byte-unixbench/pull/127))

items.title: Avoid repeated sorting when tracking shared extents
items.body:
## Summary

- keep shared physical extents sorted and merged as each range is added
- use binary search to find only the ranges affected by an insertion
- remove the full-list sort previously performed for every shared extent
- cover out-of-order insertion and adjacency merging
- log startup phase boundaries and durations at info level
- run the initial resource-monitoring snapshot asynchronously so startup no longer blocks on the disk scan; the metrics callback already skips reporting until the first snapshot exists

Resource monitoring scans reflinked snapshot extents synchronously during startup. Re-sorting every accumulated range for every extent caused startup work to grow superlinearly as snapshot trees became larger and more fragmented.

## Performance

For 10,000 disjoint sequential extents on AMD EPYC:

- before: ~170 ms/op, 30,018 allocations
- after: ~0.5 ms/op, 20 allocations

## Tests

- `go test -race ./lib/diskutilization`
- `go vet ./lib/diskutilization`
- randomized reference comparison against byte-level coverage
- `go test ./...` attempted; unrelated packages could not complete because embedded binaries are absent from the checkout and Docker Hub rejected unauthenticated test pulls. The changed package passed.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> The extent tracker algorithm changed on a hot path used during disk utilization collection; behavior is covered by new tests and benchmarks, but incorrect merging could skew shared/private byte accounting. Deferring the first monitoring refresh slightly delays metric population at startup.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Shared extent tracking** for Linux reflink/fiemap disk utilization no longer re-sorts and merges the full range list on every insertion. `sharedExtentTracker.add` uses binary search to locate affected intervals, merges overlaps in place, and keeps ranges sorted incrementally—cutting work during snapshot-tree scans that run as part of resource monitoring.
> 
> **Resource monitoring** no longer blocks `StartMonitoring` on the first `refreshMonitoringSnapshot` (which includes `diskutilization.Collect`). The initial snapshot runs inside the background loop with success/failure and duration logs; tests wait for a cached snapshot via `waitForMonitoringSnapshot`.
> 
> **API startup** adds info-level phase markers and elapsed times (overall init, OpenTelemetry, dependency wiring, resource monitoring kickoff, and total time before the HTTP server starts).

### Motivation
- Ensure rule-based benchmark policies receive the same event- and bus-level inputs assumed by the paper so their decisions match the paper definitions.
- Replace fragile evaluator lookups that could yield `E_min=0` or miss freight/ passenger dwell estimates, causing incorrect benchmark behavior.

### Description
- In `evaluate_policy`, construct an `info_ctx` passed to policies containing `T_P_est` (from `current_event.passenger_service_preview.passenger_dwell_min` when present), `T_F` (computed as `unloading_volume_kg * unloading_time_sec_per_kg / 60`), `action_mask`, and `event` context.

items.title: fix(interp): make recursive trace boundary explicit
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #184.

The Fannkuch compare benchmark could produce incorrect results in `default` and `jit` modes while `threaded` remained correct.

## Root cause

The trace recorder used `skipCall` when it encountered a recursive `CALL`. That is only sound when the recorder can model the call's effects. `skipCall` supplies placeholder return values and does not reproduce the callee's heap mutations.

A recursive call encountered inside a non-entry loop trace could therefore leave the recorder with a speculative VM/heap state that never existed. Fannkuch exposes this because its recursive permutation routine mutates a shared array and continues execution after the call.

## Fix

Treat recursive calls in non-entry loop traces as a trace boundary. The native prefix is retained, the real recursive call executes through the threaded path, and the post-call continuation can be captured from the actual frame and heap state.

Function-entry self-recursion keeps the existing native `selfCall` path, so the fix does not disable native recursive-call lowering globally or reject heap mutation from JIT plans.

The JIT trace contract documentation is updated to describe the boundary explicitly.

## Validation

- `go test -race ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test -tags=compare -run='^$' -bench='^BenchmarkCall_Fannkuch$' -benchtime=1x -count=5`
- `git diff --check`

The Fannkuch compare benchmark passes for `default`, `threaded`, `jit`, `native`, `gpython`, and `cpython` on the ARM64 development machine.

items.title: Fix benchmark guard macros
items.body:
# Fix benchmark guard macros

## Summary

- Fix incorrect preprocessor guard for ML-DSA 87 benchmark functions in `wh_bench_mod_mldsa.c`
- Add missing `WOLFHSM_CFG_ENABLE_SERVER` guard around `wh_Bench_ServerCfgLoop()` in `wh_bench.c`

## Changes

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `benchmark/bench_modules/wh_bench_mod_mldsa.c` | Replace incorrect guard `WOLFSSL_MLDSA_NO_SIGN` with `WOLFSSL_NO_ML_DSA_87` for ML-DSA 87 benchmark section |
| `benchmark/wh_bench.c` | Wrap `wh_Bench_ServerCfgLoop()` with `#if defined(WOLFHSM_CFG_ENABLE_SERVER)` guard |

## Details

### Fix typo in ML-DSA 87 guard (`wh_bench_mod_mldsa.c`)

The wrong macro `WOLFSSL_MLDSA_NO_SIGN` was used to guard the ML-DSA 87 benchmark section. The correct macro is `WOLFSSL_NO_ML_DSA_87`, consistent with the guards used for ML-DSA 44 and ML-DSA 65 in the same file.

- **Before:** `#if !defined(WOLFSSL_MLDSA_NO_SIGN)`
- **After:** `#if !defined(WOLFSSL_NO_ML_DSA_87)`

Without this fix, defining `WOLFSSL_NO_ML_DSA_87` to disable ML-DSA 87 support would not exclude the corresponding benchmark functions from compilation.

### Guard server benchmark loop (`wh_bench.c`)

`wh_Bench_ServerCfgLoop()` uses server APIs (`wh_Server_Init`, `wh_Server_HandleRequestMessage`, etc.) and must not be compiled in configurations where server support is disabled. A stub implementation is provided under `#else` so that callers such as `_whBenchServerTask()` link cleanly without server support.

- **Before:** No guard
- **After:** Full implementation wrapped with `#if defined(WOLFHSM_CFG_ENABLE_SERVER)`; stub (returns `WH_ERROR_OK`) provided under `#else`

## Impact

- No logic changes; preprocessor guard fixes only.
- Builds with `WOLFSSL_NO_ML_DSA_87` will now correctly exclude ML-DSA 87 benchmark functions.
- Builds without `WOLFHSM_CFG_ENABLE_SERVER` will now link cleanly via the stub implementation.

items.title: Fix never-perfect-black: remove benchmark==0 guard in view.c; update rtwizard ref images
items.body:
## Problem

The `regress-remrt` test was failing because `remrt/rtsrv` (and also standalone `rt`) produced pixels with value (0,0,0) for 74 hit-pixels that the canonical benchmark reference `bench/ref/m35.pix` expected as (0,0,1).

## Root Cause

The "never perfect black" check in `src/rt/view.c` had a `benchmark==0` guard:

```c
/* Make sure it's never perfect black */
if (r==0 && g==0 && b==0 && benchmark==0)
    b = 1;
```

This guard was **incorrect**. Benchmark mode (`-B`) is designed to remove *random* effects (dithering via `bn_mathtab_constant()`) to produce reproducible pixel values. It must not change *semantic* behavior like hit-vs-miss distinguishability.

A genuine hit pixel that renders to RGB (0,0,0) is indistinguishable from a background miss for any compositing pipeline that works directly with pixel values. The `bench/ref/m35.pix` canonical reference was generated with this guard always active (verified by the Windows testing commit comment: "bench/ref/m35.pix was generated with this guard always active").

The `benchmark==0` guard was introduced by the previous agent's rtwizard fix (commit `cda784b`), which conflated two separate changes from the Windows testing session:
1. Background discrimination wrapped in `!benchmark` — correctly reverted (this broke compositing)
2. Removal of `benchmark==0` guard from "never perfect black" — **incorrectly reverted**

## Fix

**`src/rt/view.c`**: Remove the `benchmark==0` guard. The "never perfect black" protection now always applies in all rendering modes:

```c
/* Make sure it's never perfect black, even in benchmark mode.
 * A genuine hit that renders to (0,0,0) is indistinguishable
 * from a background miss for any compositing that works with
 * pixel values.  The reference image bench/ref/m35.pix was
 * generated with this guard always active.  Benchmark mode
 * removes random effects (dither) but must not change semantic
 * hit-vs-miss distinguishability. */
if (r==0 && g==0 && b==0)
    b = 1;
```

**`regress/rtwizard/m35_A_ref.pix`**, **`m35_C_ref.pix`**, **`m35_D_ref.pix`**: Regenerated reference images. The rtwizard reference images for types A, C, and D were generated with the incorrect `benchmark==0` guard in place, so they had (0,0,0) for those pixels. With the fix, these 26, 2, and 6 pixels (respectively) become (0,0,1), matching correct behavior.

## Verification

- `rt -B -M -s512 -H0 -J0 m35.g all.g`: Now produces **pixel-exact** match with `bench/ref/m35.pix` (previously 74 off-by-1)
- `regress-remrt`: **PASSES** (pixel-exact match — both sub-tests pass)
- All 8 `regress-rtwiz_m35_*` tests: **PASS** (100%)

items.title: eval: harden OpenSRE LLM judge JSON extraction
items.body:
## Summary

This PR improves the robustness of the OpenSRE evaluation pipeline by hardening how LLM judge responses are parsed and validated.

The current evaluation flow relies on extracting a JSON object from LLM outputs. However, real LLM responses are often not strictly well-formed and may include additional text, markdown fences, or malformed structures. This can lead to unstable or incorrect benchmark results.

## Problem

The existing `extract_judge_json_from_response` implementation:

- assumes a clean JSON object in the response
- does not explicitly reject JSON arrays
- can incorrectly extract partial JSON from mixed outputs
- is not tested against real-world LLM response patterns

As a result, evaluation can silently succeed with incorrect parsing or fail unpredictably depending on LLM formatting.

## Changes

- Hardened JSON extraction logic:
  - captures full fenced content (not just `{...}`) to avoid partial extraction
  - explicitly rejects JSON arrays (`[...]`), including fenced cases
  - improves detection of valid JSON object boundaries
  - ensures only dictionary outputs are accepted

- Added dedicated test coverage for judge parsing:
  - clean JSON responses
  - markdown fenced JSON (```json)
  - mixed prose + JSON outputs
  - missing JSON cases
  - JSON arrays (invalid)
  - malformed JSON
  - fenced JSON arrays (invalid, now explicitly rejected)

## Why this matters

OpenSRE evaluation depends on LLM judge outputs for scoring (`overall_pass`, `score_0_100`, etc.).

This change improves:

- evaluation stability
- reproducibility of benchmark results
- robustness to real LLM output variability
- prevents silent mis-scoring due to partial JSON extraction

items.title: [BugFix][P/D] Restrict recompute scheduler to decode nodes
items.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR fixes an accuracy issue caused by enabling `recompute_scheduler_enable` on PD prefill nodes.

`recompute_scheduler_enable` is only valid on PD decode nodes. Previously, the config validation allowed it in PD-disaggregated mode for both `kv_producer` and `kv_consumer`, so some P-node launch examples and benchmark configs incorrectly enabled it. This could make the recompute scheduler take effect in an invalid role and lead to accuracy issues.

This PR:
- Rejects `recompute_scheduler_enable` unless `kv_role == "kv_consumer"`.
- Keeps the recompute scheduler disabled on PD prefill nodes and PD-mixed mode.
- Updates UT coverage for `kv_producer`, `kv_consumer`, `kv_both`, and no `kv_transfer_config`.
- Updates e2e configs and docs so `recompute_scheduler_enable` is only used on decode nodes.

Fixes #

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `recompute_scheduler_enable` now fails fast if it is configured on PD prefill nodes (`kv_role="kv_producer"`) or in PD-mixed mode. Users should enable it only on PD decode nodes (`kv_role="kv_consumer"`).

items.title: [codex] Normalize AMD Linux APU GPU names
items.body:
## Summary
- normalize Linux AMD APU GPU detection through a curated CPU-to-iGPU mapping table instead of inferring the marketed name from the CPU string
- keep the `lspci` parser reusable in a dedicated helper module and only rewrite codename or generic integrated GPU labels for single-GPU AMD systems
- add regression tests covering Phoenix3, generic `AMD Radeon Graphics`, Ryzen PRO 200-series, Ryzen AI mappings, and unmapped CPU fallbacks

## Why
Linux can report internal AMD APU codenames such as `Phoenix3` or a generic `AMD Radeon Graphics` label in the GPU slot. Those values are not stable user-facing GPU names and led to incorrect benchmark device metadata.

## Root Cause
The detector trusted raw PCI-derived AMD GPU labels too broadly. For AMD APUs, the codename alone is not enough to identify the marketed iGPU with certainty, and the previous heuristic could overfit to whatever text trailed the CPU brand string.

## Impact
The CLI now emits canonical AMD integrated GPU names such as `AMD Radeon 780M` for mapped Ryzen APUs, while leaving unknown AMD CPUs unchanged instead of guessing. That should make submitted device metadata more consistent and safer for downstream ranking and display logic.

- `bun test`

## Summary

Replaces the custom Chinese-language benchmark (hardcoded questions + LLM-as-Judge scoring) with standard authoritative benchmarks loaded from HuggingFace datasets:

- [ ] **`_load_math` boxed extraction is broken for nested braces**: `re.search(r"\\boxed\{(.+?)\}", solution)` uses a non-greedy match that will truncate answers like `\boxed{\frac{1}{2}}` to `\frac{1`. This needs a brace-balanced parser or a greedy match with backtracking. This bug affects both base and pipeline accuracy equally but will produce incorrect benchmark numbers.

### Motivation

- The previous benchmark aborted the entire suite on a single malformed stage output and reported misleading schema/compliance and category metrics. 
- The judge contract used by the benchmark deviated from the compact production `JudgeVerdict` + trusted materialization path, enabling silent repairs and invalid evidence acceptance. 
- Important-finding probe matching was conflated with semantic finding-category accuracy, producing incorrect category accuracy numbers. 
- The benchmark must preserve BlindGuard semantics and record per-case typed failures so real Codex-native runs can be trusted and audited.

### Description

- Execute every case independently and record per-case stage outcomes without aborting the suite, introducing `StageStatus` and typed `FailureCategory` to classify forward/verifier/judge/evidence/orchestration/provider failures. 
- Request the compact `JudgeVerdict` contract from the judge and materialize it with `materialize_judge_verdict(...)`, failing closed on invalid evidence rather than normalizing or repairing malformed output. 
- Replace hard-coded schema-compliance metrics with derived rates computed from actual stage attempts and successful decodes, and separate important-finding text-probe detection from true finding-category accuracy by comparing the trusted persisted verdict categories. 
- Add suite metadata (suite hash, git revision, generated timestamp), per-case execution_mode, and persist a deterministic 40-case report artifact (path: `reports/benchmark-v1/deterministic.json`); update `fixtures/evaluation/cases.json`, tests, and docs to reflect the honest execution semantics.
